edit.description: `GateContext.touchedPaths` (:132) — the shared span footprint, typed mutable under prose that states the sharing (:121-:131); the `ShipContext` sibling for the same fact (`src/Phase.ts:74`) already carries the readonly type
the second prose statement of the same claim, at `runAfterCommitGates`'s `spanTouchedPaths` doc (:636), beside the one handoff it describes (:695) and the fence gate the loop appends last (:659)
the non-vacuity read at :741, which sorts the gate's own input in place before handing that same object to the gate under test — the one in-repo site a widened type reds

summary: The span footprint every afterCommit gate is handed is one mutable array, and the shared-instance claim sits in prose at two sites while the type rung is free

per.section: Narration is the ladder's bottom rung

acceptance: `GateContext.touchedPaths` is `readonly string[]` — the rung its `ShipContext` sibling already occupies for the same fact — so the one array the gate loop hands every gate, the engine's own `writable-paths` among them, cannot be edited by one of them into what the next reads. Both prose statements of the sharing shrink to a pointer at the type in the same commit. Readers widen with it; the one in-place sort takes a copy first. The holder is `tsc` at both gate points rather than the suite: no runtime behavior changes, so the entry names no `tests[]` and no `pins[]` line. `pnpm tsc --noEmit` and `pnpm test` green.
notes: Verified on disk: nothing in `src/` or `harness/` mutates it, and the suite already copies defensively (`tests/builtinGates.test.ts:1337`, `tests/Dispatcher.test.ts:9578`) — discipline nothing checks; `:741` is the site that does not. Filed for the blast radius: the fence gate reads the list it is handed (`src/builtinGates.ts:600`-`:631`), and `src/tickAttempt.ts:762` returns that same instance as the revert footprint the ledger records.
